Options for NonsmoothNewton: Newton with a protected path on the split f = s + n of the problem (Problem::has_nonsmooth_term). On an iterate with active nonsmooth terms it minimizes a reduced model (frozen quadratic of s, exact n) with Levenberg-Marquardt steps in a growing subspace, certifies every segment of the path with max_step_size and accepts the end point (or a retraction along the path) by the true decrease; otherwise the Newton direction is line searched. Falls back to the Newton chain.
Inner step budget per outer iteration.
Stop the inner loop when a step's model decrease is below this fraction of the accumulated decrease (0 = off).
Linearized fraction-to-boundary on the active nonsmooth terms: distance >= tau * distance at the segment start (0 = off).
Acceptance ratio of the true decrease to the model decrease, in (0, 1).
Subspace column cap.

Hand the rest of the solve to the Newton chain once the true energy can no longer verify the path: any = after an outer iteration whose inner loop stopped at the noise floor of the energy or whose path is below the energy resolution; first = only if this happened before any inner step was accepted; off = never. Except for off, also when the gradient norm is below line_search/use_grad_norm_tol, measured as the line search measures it for its switch to comparing gradient norms instead of energies (norm_type and its rescaling); see hand_back for the way back from this one.

Take 32 eps |E| as the resolution of the true energy E: the inner noise floor includes it, and a path whose model decrease does not exceed it is not verified by the true energy (the Newton step is line searched instead).

Hand-back after a handoff on a small gradient (see handoff): the first step of the Newton chain that ends above the gradient tolerance, removes more than energy times the energy resolution 32 eps |E| (E before the step) and is slow hands the iterations back to NonsmoothNewton. Slow: cut by its line search (step size < 1), taken by a strategy at index >= 2 of the solver (behind Newton: projected Newton or later in the default chain), or reducing the gradient norm (the norm of the stopping test) less than contraction times. The handoff on a small gradient is then off for the rest of the solve, so it happens at most once per solve; the handoff after a noise-floor stop is unchanged. NonsmoothNewton resumes at the next iteration the solver gives to its first strategy.
Enable the hand-back.
Energy decrease of the chain step, in units of the energy resolution 32 eps |E|, above which a slow step hands back.
Gradient norm reduction a chain step must reach not to count as slow.

Limits on the element volume ratios J = det F of the smooth part at the end point y of every inner step (after its Armijo test), checked in one sweep over the elements through Problem::smooth_min_jacobians. They keep the path where the frozen quadratic of the smooth part is trusted: for an energy term -log J, once an outer iteration needs an element compressed below half its volume, the minimizer of the element's quadratic model is an inverted configuration. If a step after the first violates a limit, the path ends at the previous point; if the first step does, it is halved further (at most 40 times) until the limits and the Armijo test hold, and the path ends after it (no such point: no inner step, the Newton step is line searched). A limit is not applied where the problem gives NaN (the defaults of Problem::smooth_min_jacobian(s)); that is reported once per solve at debug level.
Every element keeps J_e(y) >= bound * J_e(x), x the outer iterate (0 = off).

The smallest J over the elements stays >= floor * J_ref, or >= its value at the outer iterate where that is already lower (0 = off). J_ref is the smallest J at the first iterate of the solve whose direction request NonsmoothNewton does not decline by the handoff (and where the problem gives a finite value); if the solve starts below the gradient threshold of the handoff, that is the first iterate after a hand-back, not the start of the solve.

Jg: gate the relative Jacobian limit on the exact units by its effect (a limit that ended a path pays if the next outer iteration has no limit event itself). auto = off for the energy split, gate for the blind selection.
Window of the gate.

Which units of the problem are modelled exactly by the path: energy_split = the nonsmooth term n that the problem gives; blind = units chosen by the problem's selection (NonsmoothTerm::selection).
Protected path.
Run the path at every outer iteration, not only where nonsmooth terms are active. auto = off for the energy split, on for the blind selection.
Units that the path promotes to the nonsmooth term when a limiter cuts a step.

Enable the promotion: the units behind a step cut by a limiter (fraction-to-boundary, max_step_size, Jacobian limits) become exact in place and the path restarts. auto = off for the energy split, on for the blind selection.
How a promoted unit enters the model: exact, frozen (the anchor's block) or frozen_projected (the projected block of B).
How a promoted unit enters B: projected or raw. frozen with raw lifts nothing and is an error.
Largest number of restarts of the path after promotions in one outer iteration.
Keep the model value continuous across a restart (needs reread).
Re-read of the true gradient at the inner points of the path.
Enable the re-read of the true gradient at the inner points. auto = off for the energy split, on for the blind selection.
Threshold on the gradient before the handoff on a small gradient.

Hand the solve to the Newton chain after a noise-floor stop only if 1/2 g.B^-1 g at the anchor is at most factor times the energy resolution (else the path is tried again, at most max_refusals times without progress). auto = off for the energy split, on for the blind selection.
Factor of the threshold.
Largest number of refusals of a handoff.
Algebra of the reduced model.

Reduced algebra of the model: the gradient of the reduced model sums only the rows of the nonsmooth gradient that can be nonzero (instead of forming the full-length vector and multiplying by the basis), and G is formed again from H Q when units move. Changes rounding. Platform option, default off.
Keep a row-major copy of the basis columns for the row gathers of the reduced model (same values, contiguous rows). Platform option, default off.
Assembly of the reduced matrix of the model.
per_block = block by block; merged = one merged product; auto = merged from merged_min_blocks blocks at the first point of an outer iteration.
Number of blocks from which auto uses the merged product.
Repair of the basis matrix when its factorization fails.
off or r_ad (local repair). Only off is available yet.
Largest number of repair rounds.
Radius of the repaired neighbourhood in the node graph.
Limiters whose cut promotes units: jfloor, jbound (Jacobian limits), ftb (fraction-to-boundary), ccd (max_step_size). A validity cut does not promote.
One limiter of first_layer/events.
Parameters of the blind selection (selection = blind); read by the problem implementation.
Second layer: at the start of an outer iteration the units with the largest force error become exact (within a budget).
Enable the second layer.
Budget of the second layer: the force error that stays frozen is at most eta times the larger residual of the two anchors.
Marginal benefit: a batch of units is admitted only if it lowers the remaining error by more than this relative amount (0 = off).
Third layer: units stay exact across time steps while they are charged.
Enable the third layer (units that were charged in the last epoch stay in the exact set).
Only units that are present at both anchors are charged with a force error.
A unit that is born exact (a new contact pair) stays exact while it is present, whatever the third layer says.
Where exact units that were not charged leave the exact set: at every change of the energy (all_changes) or only at time steps (time_step).
How the local energy terms are grouped into units: local_term (terms that depend on the same nodes form one unit).

What to do with an energy form that cannot be split into units: error (stop at startup, naming the form) or remainder (the form stays in the frozen part: its gradient and Hessian at the anchor; it is not a unit and is never selected).
augmented Lagrangian subproblems: newton (the Newton chain solves them) or blind.
A time step after one whose inner steps were cut by limiters too often skips the second and third layer.
